summary: HydroGuard SAR is an open-source geospatial intelligence platform powered by NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR L2 GCOV) data and meteorological archives to detect undocumented water reservoirs (hillside retention basins) and clandestine agricultural irrigation during drought restriction periods. Optical satellites fail when clouds or dense crop canopies obscure the ground, and environmental agencies lack the field staff to inspect thousands of private agricultural parcels. Using 24 cm L-band polarimetric radar (HHHH and HVHV), our Python pipeline penetrates clouds and vegetation to identify specular reflection drops from newly filled reservoirs alongside sudden soil dielectric spikes from clandestine irrigation, cross-checking every anomaly against zero-rainfall meteorological logs. Through an interactive 3D Earth globe and a local Optical-vs-SAR X-Ray wipe explorer, water regulators can instantly pinpoint priority GPS coordinates and protect stressed aquifers and river ecosystems.
details:
HydroGuard SAR is an open-source geospatial intelligence web platform powered by NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR L2 GCOV) data and meteorological archives to detect undocumented water reservoirs (hillside retention basins) and clandestine agricultural irrigation during drought restriction periods.

- L-Band Polarimetric Change Detection (Python Pipeline): Our processing script ingests co-registered NISAR_L2_PR_GCOV HDF5 granules (HHHH and HVHV polarizations at 24 cm L-band wavelength) acquired across the same orbital track before and during summer drought bans. After radiometric calibration to decibels (dB) and spatial speckle filtering, the algorithm isolates two physical microwave signatures across flat agricultural plains:
1) Newly Filled Reservoirs & Basins (Cyan): Detected via specular reflection drops (HH2 < -17.0 dB and ΔHH < -2.8 dB), where rough dry land turns into a smooth water mirror.
2) Soil Moisture & Irrigation Spikes (Amber): Detected via sudden dielectric constant increases (ΔHH between +2.3 dB and +6.0 dB), as L-band microwaves penetrate crop canopies (such as corn or orchards) to sense wet soil underneath.
- Parcel Vectorization & Meteorological Cross-Validation: Detected clusters are filtered by morphological compactness to eliminate terrain or radar noise and vectorized into lightweight GeoJSON polygons (parcels_alert.geojson) alongside hectare statistics (stats_water.json). Each radar anomaly is cross-checked against historical precipitation records (0 mm rainfall during drought bans) to rule out natural rain events.
- Interactive 3D Globe & Optical/SAR X-Ray Explorer: Users start on an interactive 3D Orbital Globe where they can search any city or click anywhere on Earth, transitioning into a high-resolution local map featuring a pixel-accurate Optical vs. NISAR SAR X-Ray Wipe, layer toggles, priority inspection alerts with direct satellite coordinates, and rainfall charts.

What benefits does it have?
- All-Weather, Day-and-Night Monitoring: Unlike optical satellites that are blinded by cloud cover or dense crop foliage, NISAR's L-band radar penetrates clouds and vegetation every 12 days, catching nighttime or overcast water pumping.
- Massive Time & Cost Savings for Water Authorities: Environmental agencies lack the field staff to inspect tens of thousands of private agricultural parcels on foot. HydroGuard SAR narrows down vast watersheds to top-priority GPS coordinates in seconds.
- Irrefutable Dual-Source Evidence: Combining radar dielectric changes with zero-rainfall meteorological logs provides objective, timestamped proof of human water extraction rather than natural precipitation.

HydroGuard SAR aims to protect freshwater ecosystems, aquifers, and river basins facing severe summer droughts. By giving water regulators, regional prefectures, and environmental organizations an accessible early-warning dashboard, the platform helps enforce drought restriction decrees fairly, prevents illegal depletion of groundwater tables, and preserves water availability for drinking water supplies, biodiversity, and compliant farmers.


- NASA & Geospatial Data: NASA-ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV products via Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF Data Search Vertex), Esri World Imagery basemaps, and Komoot Photon / OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocoding APIs.
- Data Processing Pipeline (Backend): Python 3.11, h5py (HDF5 parsing), NumPy, SciPy (uniform_filter speckle reduction and connected-component parcel labeling), PyProj (EPSG coordinate transformations to WGS84), and GeoJSON/JSON serialization.
- Web Application (Frontend): HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), Globe.gl / Three.js (3D interactive Earth), Leaflet.js (custom vector panes and pixel-aligned clip-path X-Ray wipe), and Chart.js (precipitation timeline).
- Development & Deployment: Visual Studio Code, Git & GitHub (open-source repository), and Netlify (cloud hosting).
- Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure: Large language models (Google Gemini) were used solely to assist with code debugging, structuring the web interface, and drafting project documentation. No SI-generated images, audio, or NASA logos/branding were created or modified.

- Making SAR Readable for Non-Experts ("X-Ray Vision"): Raw radar backscatter images in grayscale are difficult for decision-makers and citizens to interpret. We translated complex polarimetric decibel shifts (ΔHH and HV) into clean, color-coded agricultural parcel polygons paired with an interactive vertical optical vs. radar SAR wipe, letting anyone visually compare an innocent-looking green field in optical view with its glowing water-saturated radar signature.
- From Global Scale to Actionable Field Inspection: Rather than limiting users to static screenshots, we combined a global 3D Earth interface with direct field-audit links that take an inspector straight to high-resolution satellite coordinates.

What we considered:
- Real-World Operational Need: Inspired by summer water conflicts and unauthorized hillside reservoirs in agricultural regions such as southwestern France (Occitanie), we focused on a problem where physical on-foot inspection is impossible at scale and optical imagery fails.
- Eliminating False Positives: Steep mountain slopes, urban buildings, and radar speckle can mimic backscatter changes. Our team incorporated terrain/cross-polarization masking, spatial multi-look averaging, compactness thresholds, and rainfall cross-checking to ensure alerts correspond to genuine flat agricultural parcels or retention basins.
- Web Performance & Open-Source Accessibility: Because raw NISAR .h5 granules exceed 1.8 GB each, we decoupled heavy scientific processing in Python from a lightweight static frontend (< 1 MB GeoJSON/JSON), allowing the web app to run smoothly on any browser.
